events.title: Treaty of Paris Signed
events.description: Representatives of Great Britain and the United States signed the Treaty of Paris in Paris, formally ending the American Revolutionary War. Britain recognized the independence of the United States and defined its boundaries.
events.significance: The treaty established the United States as a sovereign nation and set its territorial borders, reshaping the balance of power in North America.

events.title: Britain and France Declare War on Germany
events.description: Two days after Germany invaded Poland, Britain and France declared war on Nazi Germany, honoring their guarantees to Poland. Australia and New Zealand also declared war the same day.
events.significance: This marked the formal beginning of World War II in Europe, drawing major world powers into a global conflict that lasted until 1945.

events.title: Allied Invasion of Italy Begins
events.description: British Eighth Army forces landed on the Italian mainland at Calabria in Operation Baytown. On the same day, Italy secretly signed the Armistice of Cassibile with the Allies.
events.significance: The invasion opened a new front in Europe and led to Italy's withdrawal from the Axis, though the Germans occupied much of the country and fighting continued for nearly two more years.

events.title: Death of Oliver Cromwell
events.description: Oliver Cromwell, Lord Protector of England, Scotland, and Ireland, died of illness on the anniversary of his victories at Dunbar and Worcester. His son Richard succeeded him.
events.significance: Cromwell's death led to the collapse of the Protectorate and paved the way for the restoration of the monarchy under Charles II in 1660.

events.title: Coronation of Richard I
events.description: Richard the Lionheart was crowned King of England at Westminster Abbey. The occasion was marred by anti-Jewish riots in London that spread to other parts of England.
events.significance: Richard's reign was dominated by the Third Crusade, and his long absences from England shaped the political developments that later led to Magna Carta under his brother John.
